messages:
jonathan: heads up — noticed some strange quota attribution for requests routed with the new route-intent tag. console shows tokens charged to 'default' bucket even when route-intent is set.

maya: where are you seeing this? which environment?

jonathan: staging, repro steps: hitting /v1/generate with header `X-Route-Intent: analytics:high` + sdk-ts v2.1.0. console shows route mapping = analytics but quota ledger gets folded into default.cost-center.

li: interesting. can you paste a raw request (strip api key) and a sample trace id?

jonathan: sure — trace id 000abcd. request snippet: ```
POST /v1/generate
Host: api.redwood.example
Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>
X-Route-Intent: analytics:high
Content-Type: application/json
{ "model": "rw-large", "input": "..." }
```

eva: quick thought — we recently normalized header casing in the python/ts sdk clients to avoid duplicate headers (BREAKING?). Might be that the console routing layer expects the route-intent header in dashed-lowercase but our SDK now sends `x-route-intent` and intermediate proxy normalizes to `x-route_intent` (ugh).

ryan: i can check proxy logs. if proxy rewrites header names we should still have routing metadata in the raw request context. maybe the console's attribution stage is doing a strict header lookup.

maya: feel like two fixes: 1) make server-side header matching case-insensitive + accept underscore variants; 2) SDK publish a tiny patch that preserves the original header name or sets canonical `Route-Intent` header. both easy, we should decide order.

li: +1 on server fix first. it's safer. i'll open a quick PR to the routing-service to search header keys by normalized form (lowercase, dashes/underscores both accepted).

jonathan: sounds good. for immediate unblock i patched our staging proxy to copy `x-route_intent` -> `x-route-intent` and it fixed attribution.

eva: thanks. separate but related: the python SDK 1.3.x also started compressing telemetry envelope fields which removed route metadata unless you opt-in. that's why some tests in CI flaked. we need a doc blurb in the release notes.

ryan: i found proxy logs referencing trace 000abcd — proxy did replace dashes with underscores when header came from internal grpc path. i'm adding a test to ensure header passthrough for routing headers.

maya: can we also include a console dashboard alert rule for atypical quota folding (i.e., >90% attributed to default when route-intent header present)? That will catch regressions sooner.

jonathan: yes please. created a quick jira: PLAT-8293 — dashboard alert + routing-service fix + sdk patch. tagging devex for a short release-note.

deploy-bot: canary deployed routing-service PR #567 to staging at 2025-11-03T09:12:00Z :rocket:

li: PR linked in jira. i'll cut a small changelist tomorrow and ping @devex for release note copy.

eva: for release note include the workaround snippet for TS/Python: ```ts
// TS workaround if you can't upgrade right away
fetch(url, { headers: { 'X-Route-Intent': 'analytics:high', 'x-route-intent': 'analytics:high' } })
```
```py
# Python workaround
headers = { 'X-Route-Intent': 'analytics:high', 'x-route_intent': 'analytics:high' }
client.request(..., headers=headers)
```

ryan: will follow up with a tiny unit test in proxy repo and a console metric to show how many requests have both variants present.

jonathan: thanks all — marking staging as green now. i'll retest tomorrow after the server-side normalization lands. :thumbsup:
